senses.definition: The fruit of the tree Malus domestica, chiefly with a green, red, or yellow skin, cultivated in temperate climates for cidermaking, cooking, and eating.

senses.definition: Often with a qualifying word: any fruit or vegetable, or any other thing (such as a cone or gall) produced by a plant, especially if from a tree and similar to the fruit of Malus domestica (noun sense 1.1).
Something which resembles the fruit of Malus domestica (noun sense 1.1) in shape (such as a ball, breast, or globe) or colour.
The round, fleshy part of a cheek between the eye and the corner of the mouth when a person is smiling.
The surface of revolution of a circular arc of an angle greater than 180° rotated about the straight line passing through the arc's two endpoints.
In full apple bowl: a round bowl of a tobacco pipe; also, a tobacco pipe with such a bowl.
In full old apple: a baseball.
According to postbiblical Christian tradition, the fruit of the tree of knowledge which was eaten by Adam and Eve despite God commanding them not to do so; the forbidden fruit.
Synonym of pome (“a type of fruit in which the often edible flesh arises from the swollen base of the flower and not from the carpels”).
An imaginary diminutive unit of height.
A tree of the genus Malus; especially Malus domestica which is cultivated for its edible fruit; the apple tree.

senses.definition: The seed-bearing part of a plant; often edible, colourful, fragrant, and sweet or sour; produced from a floral ovary after fertilization.
The spores of cryptogams and their accessory organs.
Any sweet or sour, edible part of a plant that resembles seed-bearing fruit (see former sense) even if it does not develop from a floral ovary.
A sweet or sweetish vegetable, such as the petioles of rhubarb, that resembles a true fruit or is used in cookery as if it was a fruit.
An end result, effect, or consequence; advantageous or disadvantageous result.
Of, belonging to, related to, or having fruit or its characteristics; (of living things) producing or consuming fruit.
A homosexual man, especially an effeminate one.
An effeminate man.
Offspring from a sexual union.
A crazy person.

senses.definition: The act of preserving, guarding, or protecting; the keeping (of a thing) in a safe or entire state; preservation.

lack of change in a measurable property of an isolated physical system (conservation of energy, mass, momentum, electric charge, subatomic particles, and fundamental symmetries)

etymology.text: From Middle English happy (“fortunate, happy”), perhaps an alteration of Middle English happyn, happen (“fortunate, happy”), possibly related to or from Old Norse heppinn (“fortunate, happy”); and potentially assimilated to be equivalent to hap (“chance, luck, fortune”) + -y. Compare also Icelandic heppinn (“lucky”), Faroese heppin (“fortunate, lucky, happy”), Norwegian Nynorsk heppen (“lucky”), Scots happin (“fortunate, blessed”). See further at hap.
etymology.native: 「happy」源自中古英語 hapyn 或 happen，意為「幸運、幸福」，可能與古諾斯語 heppinn（意為「幸運」）有關；也可能與 hap（意為「機會、運氣」）+ -y 結合而成。可參照冰島語 heppinn（意為「幸運」）、法羅語 heppin（意為「幸運、幸福」）、挪威語 Nynorsk heppen（意為「幸運」）及蘇格蘭語 happin（意為「幸運、祝福」）。詳見 hap。

senses.definition: Emitting much light; visually dazzling; luminous, lucent, radiant.
Of light: brilliant, intense.
Of an object, surface, etc.: reflecting much light; having a high lustre; gleaming, shiny.
Of a place: not dark; well-lit.
Of climate or weather: not cloudy or gloomy; fair; also, of a period of time, the sky, etc.: characterized by much sunshine and good weather.
Clearly apparent; conspicuous.
Of a colour: not muted or pale; bold, brilliant, vivid.
Of an object, surface, etc.: having vivid colour(s); colourful.
Of a musical instrument, sound, or a voice: clearly audible; clear, resounding, and often high-pitched.

etymology.text: From Middle English bred, breed, from Old English brēad (“fragment, bit, morsel, crumb", also "bread”), from Proto-West Germanic *braud, from Proto-Germanic *braudą (“bread”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerw-, *bʰrewh₁- (“to boil; to brew”), from *bʰer- (“to bear, carry”). Alternatively, from Proto-Germanic *braudaz, *brauþaz (“broken piece, fragment”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰera- (“to split, beat, hew, struggle”) (see brittle). Perhaps a conflation of the two. Possibly a doublet of broa.
etymology.native: 「bread」源自中世英文的 bred、breed，來自古英文 brēad（意為「碎片、小塊、碎屑」，亦指「麵包」），再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *braud，來自原始日耳曼語 *braudą（意為「麵包」），再往上溯源自原始印歐語 *bʰerw-、*bʰrewh₁-（意為「煮沸、發酵」），而 *bʰer-（意為「承載、攜帶」）。另一說法源自原始日耳曼語 *braudaz、*brauþaz（意為「破碎的片段」），來自原始印歐語 *bʰera-（意為「劈開、敲打、切割」）（見 brittle）。可能為兩者融合而成，也可能為 broa 的同源詞。

etymology.text: From Middle English malencolie, from Old French melancolie, from Ancient Greek μελαγχολία (melankholía, “atrabiliousness”) (from μέλας (mélas), μελαν- (melan-, “black, dark, murky”) + χολή (kholḗ, “bile”)), referring to the humour which ancient Hippocratic and later Galenic medicine associated with sadness and despondency. Compare the Latin ātra bīlis (“black bile”). The adjectival use is a Middle English innovation, perhaps influenced by the suffixes -y, -ly. Doublet of melancholia.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 malencolie，來自古法文 melancolie，再來自古希臘文 μελαγχολία（melankholía，意為「憂鬱」），此詞由 μέλας（mélas，意為「黑、暗、混濁」）與 χολή（kholḗ，意為「膽汁」）組成，指古代希波克拉底與蓋倫醫學所稱與悲傷與低落相關的體液。與拉丁文 ātra bīlis（「黑膽汁」）相對。形容詞用法為中世紀英文創新，可能受 -y、-ly 等後綴影響。此詞亦為 melancholia 的同源詞。

etymology.text: From Middle English *ocean, occean, occian, occyan, from Old French occean (later reborrowed or reinforced by Middle French ocean), from Latin Ōceanus, originally from Ancient Greek Ὠκεανός (Ōkeanós, “Oceanus”, a water deity). Displaced native Old English gārseċġ. Also commonly referred to as the ocean sea, the sea of ocean (compare Latin mare ōceanum; Old French mer oceane, occeanne mer). Compare Saterland Frisian Oceoan (“ocean”), West Frisian oseaan (“ocean”), Dutch oceaan (“ocean”), German L

etymology.text: From Middle English wynd, wind, from Old English wind (“wind”), from Proto-West Germanic *wind, from Proto-Germanic *windaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wéh₁n̥tos (“wind”), from earlier *h₂wéh₁n̥ts (“wind”), derived from the present participle of *h₂weh₁- (“to blow”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 wynd，意為「風」，來自古英文 wind（「風」），再溯源自古西日耳曼語 *wind，更上溯至古德語 *windaz，再往上溯至印歐語系 *h₂wéh₁n̥tos，源自更早的 *h₂wéh₁n̥ts，由 *h₂weh₁-（「吹」）的現在分詞衍生。

senses.definition: To offer a view (of something) from a higher position.
To fail to notice; to look over and beyond (anything) without seeing it.
To pretend not to have noticed (something, especially a mistake or flaw); to pass over (something) without censure or punishment.
To look down upon from above or from a higher location.
To supervise, oversee; to watch over.
To observe or watch (someone or something) surreptitiously or secretly.
To inspect (something); to examine; to look over carefully or repeatedly.
To look upon with an evil eye; to bewitch by looking upon; to fascinate.

etymology.text: From pot + -ed. Adjective meaning "prepared in advance" by analogy with potted meat (canned meat), first used in a published work by L. Susan Stebbing in her Pelican classic Thinking to some purpose (1939), where "potted thinking" is defined as "a compressed statement to save us the trouble of thinking".
etymology.native: 由 pot + -ed 派生，形容詞意為「提前準備」，類比於罐裝肉，最早見於 L. Susan Stebbing 1939 年出版的《Thinking to some purpose》一書，其中定義「potted thinking」為「簡化之語句，省去我們思考之苦」。

etymology.text: From Middle English wet (“wet, moistened”), wett, wette, past participle of Middle English weten (“to wet”), from Old English wǣtan (“to wet, moisten, water”), from Proto-West Germanic *wātijan, from Proto-Germanic *wētijaną (“to wet, make wet”), from Proto-Indo-European *wed- (“water, wet”) (also the source of water).
etymology.native: 「wet」源自中世紀英文，意為「濕、浸溼」，是中世紀英文「wet」的過去分詞，而「wet」本身來自古英文「wǣtan」，意為「濕、浸溼、澆水」，再往上溯源於原始西日耳曼語「*wātijan」，源自原始日耳曼語「*wētijaną」，最後來自原始印歐語「*wed-」，意為「水、濕」，亦為「water」的語源。

etymology.text: From Late Middle English brik, bryke, bricke, from Middle Low German and Middle Dutch bricke ("cracked or broken brick; tile-stone"; modern Dutch brik), ultimately related to Proto-West Germanic *brekan (“to break”), whence also Old French briche and French brique (“brick”). Compare also German Low German Brickje (“small board, tray”). Related to break.
etymology.native: 來自中古英語 brik, bryke, bricke，源自低德語與中荷蘭語 bricke（意為「破裂的磚塊或瓦片」；現代荷蘭語 brik），最終源自古西德語 *brekan（意為「打破」），亦見於法語 briche 與 brique。亦可參見德語低德語 Brickje（意為「小木板或托盤」）。與 break 有關。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English schade, from Old English sċeadu, from Proto-West Germanic *skadu, from Proto-Germanic *skaduz, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱh₃tús, from *(s)ḱeh₃-. Doublet of shadow. Cognate with Ancient Greek σκότος (skótos) (whence English scoto-) and σκιά (skiá) (whence English scia-, and uncertainly via σκίουρος (skíouros) English squirrel).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 schade，來源為古英語 sċeadu，再溯自原始西日耳曼語 *skadu，再溯自原始德語 *skaduz，再溯自原始印歐語 *(s)ḱh₃tús，源自 *(s)ḱeh₃-。為 shadow 的同源詞。與古希臘語 σκότος (skótos)（由此衍生英文 scoto-）及 σκιά (skiá)（由此衍生英文 scia-，並可能經 σκίουρος (skíouros) 產生英文 squirrel）同源。

senses.definition: The spectral composition of visible light.

images.author: THOR
images.attribution: originally posted to Flickr as Spoon Collection

senses.definition: A particular set of visible spectral compositions, perceived or named as a class.
Hue as opposed to achromatic colors (black, white and grays).
These hues as used in color television or films, color photographs, etc (as opposed to the shades of grey used in black-and-white television).
Any of the standard dark tinctures used in a coat of arms, including azure, gules, sable, and vert.
A paint.
Human skin tone, especially as an indicator of race or ethnicity.
Skin color, noted as normal, jaundiced, cyanotic, flush, mottled, pale, or ashen as part of the skin signs assessment.
A flushed appearance of blood in the face; redness of complexion.
Richness of expression; detail or flavour that is likely to generate interest or enjoyment.

senses.definition: The denotation, referent, or idea connected with a word, expression, or symbol.
The connotation associated with a word, expression, or symbol.
The purpose, value, or significance (of something) beyond the fact of that thing's existence.
Intention.

etymology.text: From Middle English mening, menyng, equivalent to mean + -ing. Cognate with Scots mening (“intent, purpose, sense, meaning”), West Frisian miening (“opinion, mind”), Dutch mening (“view, opinion, judgement”), German Meinung (“opinion, view, mind, idea”), Danish and Swedish mening (“meaning, sense, sentence, opinion”), Icelandic meining (“meaning”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 mening、menyng，意為 mean + -ing。與蘇格蘭語 mening（意為「意圖、目的、意義」）、西弗里斯蘭語 miening（意為「意見、心思」）、荷蘭語 mening（意為「觀點、意見、判斷」）、德語 Meinung（意為「意見、觀點、心思、想法」）、丹麥語與瑞典語 mening（意為「意義、語意、句子、意見」）、冰島語 meining（意為「意義」）同源。

senses.definition: A flat open area on the topmost floor of a building or apartment
A platform that extends outwards from a building.
A raised, flat-topped bank of earth with sloping sides, especially one of a series for farming or leisure; a similar natural area of ground, often next to a river.
A step-like landform; (sometimes) remnants of floodplains.
A row of residential houses with no gaps between them; a group of row houses.
A street with such a group of houses in it.
A single house in such a group.
The standing area of a sports stadium.
The roof of a building, especially if accessible to the residents. Often used for drying laundry, sun-drying foodstuffs, exercise, or sleeping outdoors in hot weather.
A champagne, (an ordinary occupying) the base of the shield.

The office or dignity of a judge.

etymology.text: From Middle English bench, benk, bynk, from Old English benċ (“bench”), from Proto-West Germanic *banki, from Proto-Germanic *bankiz (“bench”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeg-.
etymology.native: 「bench」源自中世紀英文，由古英語 benċ 來源，而古英語 benċ 又源自古西日耳曼語 *banki，再往上溯源自古德語 *bankiz，最終可追溯至印歐語系 *bʰeg-。

etymology.text: From Middle English gardyn, garden, from Anglo-Norman gardin, from Frankish *gardin-, oblique stem of *gardō (“enclosure, yard”), from Proto-Germanic *gardô (“enclosure, garden, house”), whence also inherited English yard. (compare Old French jart alongside jardin, Medieval Latin gardīnus). Doublet of jardin and of garth. Displaced Old English wyrttūn.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 gardyn，意為「花園」，來自盎格魯-諾曼語 gardin，再源自古法語 *gardin-，為 *gardō（「圍欄、院子」）的偏正形式，而 *gardō 又源自古德語 *gardô（「圍欄、花園、房屋」），此詞亦傳入英文 yard。可與古法文 jart 及中世紀拉丁文 gardīnus 相對照。為 jardin 與 garth 的同源詞，亦取代了古英語 wyrttūn。

etymology.text: From Middle English knyf, knif, from late Old English cnīf, from Old Norse knífr or Proto-West Germanic *knīb, from Proto-Germanic *knībaz, from *knīpaną (“to pinch”), Proto-Indo-European *gneybʰ- (compare Lithuanian gnýbti, žnýbti (“to pinch”), gnaibis (“pinching”)). Displaced native Middle English sax (“knife”), from Old English seax; and Middle English coutel, qwetyll (“knife”) from Old French coutel.
etymology.native: 「knife」源自中古英語 knyf、knif，來源為古英語 cnīf，再溯自古諾斯語 knífr 或古西德語 *knīb，源自古德語 *knībaz，而 *knīpaną（意為「捏」），再溯自印歐語系 *gneybʰ-（可比擬立陶宛語 gnýbti、žnýbti（意為「捏」）、gnaibis（意為「捏」））。此詞取代了中古英語原生詞 sax（刀），源自古英語 seax；以及中古英語 coutel、qwetyll（刀），源自法語 coutel。

etymology.text: From Middle English plate, from Old French plate, from Medieval Latin plata, from Vulgar Latin *plat(t)us, from Ancient Greek πλατύς (platús, “broad, flat, wide”). Compare Spanish plato.
etymology.native: 「plate」源自中世紀英語，來源於古法語 plate，再源自中世紀拉丁語 plata，源自通俗拉丁語 *plat(t)us，最終來自古希臘語 πλατύς（platús），意為「寬廣、平坦」。可與西班牙語 plato 相比。

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English table, tabel, tabil, tabul, from Old English tabele, tabul, tablu, tabule, tabula (“board”); also as tæfl, tæfel, an early Germanic borrowing of Latin tabula (“tablet, board, plank, chart”). The sense of “piece of furniture” is from Old French table, of same Latin origin; Old English used bēod or bord instead for this meaning: see board. Doublet of tabula and tavla.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 table、tabel、tabil、tabul，來自古英語 tabele、tabul、tablu、tabule、tabula（意為「板」）；亦作 tæfl、tæfel，為拉丁文 tabula（意為「平板、板、木板、圖表」）的早期日耳曼語借詞。作為「家具」之義，源自法語 table，同源拉丁語；古英語用 bēod 或 bord 表達此義，詳見 board。為 tabula 與 tavla 的同義詞。

etymology.text: From Middle English sclise, sklise, from Old French esclice, esclis (“a piece split off”), deverbal of esclicer, esclicier (“to splinter, split up”), from Frankish *slitjan (“to split up”), from Proto-Germanic *slitjaną, from Proto-Germanic *slītaną (“to split, tear apart”), from Proto-Indo-European *sleyd- (“to rend, injure, crumble”). Akin to Old High German sliz, gisliz (“a tear, rip”), Old High German slīȥan (“to tear”), Old English slītan (“to split up”), modern French éclisse. More at slit
etymology.native: 此詞源自中世英文 sclise, sklise，來自古法文 esclice, esclis（意為「分離出的一塊」），為動詞 esclicer, esclicier（意為「劈開、分開」）的來源，而該動詞又源自古弗蘭克語 *slitjan（意為「劈開」），再溯源自古日耳曼語 *slitjaną，再往上溯源自古日耳曼語 *slītaną（意為「劈開、撕裂」），最終源自印歐語系 *sleyd-（意為「撕裂、損傷、粉碎」）。與古高地德語 sliz, gisliz（意為「撕裂、裂口」）、古高地德語 slīȥan（意為「撕裂」）、古英語 slītan（意為「劈開」）、現代法文 éclisse 同源。詳見 slit

etymology.text: From Middle English crome, cromme, crumme, crume, from Old English cruma (“crumb, fragment”), from Proto-Germanic *krumô, *krūmô (“fragment, crumb”). The b is unetymological, as in limb, and first appeared in the mid-15th century, influenced by crumble and words such as dumb, numb, and thumb. Cognate with Dutch kruim (“crumb”), Low German Krome, Krume (“crumb”), German Krume (“crumb”), Danish krumme (“crumb”), Swedish dialectal krumma (“crumb”), Swedish in kråm (“crumbs, giblets”), Icelandic kru
etymology.native: crome、cromme、crumme、crume 來自古英語 cruma（碎屑），源自原始日耳曼語 *krumô、*krūmô（碎屑、碎粒）。b 字無來源，見於 limb，最早出現於 15 世紀中葉，受 crumble 及 dumb、numb、thumb 等詞影響。與荷蘭語 kruim（碎屑）、低德語 Krome、Krume（碎屑）、德語 Krume（碎屑）、丹麥語 krumme（碎屑）、瑞典方言 krumma（碎屑）、瑞典語 kråm（碎屑、內臟）、冰島語 kru 相關。

senses.definition: An organism that is not an animal, especially an organism capable of photosynthesis, and typically a small or herbaceous organism of this kind, rather than a tree.

An organism of the kingdom Plantae, and now specifically, a living organism of the Embryophyta (land plants) or of the Chlorophyta (green algae), a eukaryote that includes double-membraned chloroplasts in its cells containing chlorophyll a and b, or any organism closely related to such an organism.
Now specifically, a multicellular eukaryote that includes chloroplasts in its cells, which have a cell wall.
A young tree, vine, shrub, or herb; a sapling.
Any creature that grows on soil or similar surfaces, including plants and fungi.
A factory or other industrial or institutional building or facility.
Machinery and other supplies and equipment, such as the kind used in heavy industry, light industry, earthmoving, or construction.
The equipment and work animals of a drover or other rural worker travelling through the countryside.
An object placed surreptitiously in order to cause suspicion to fall upon a person.
A stash or cache of hidden goods.
Anyone assigned to behave as a member of the public during a covert operation (as in a police investigation).

etymology.text: From Middle English forke (“digging fork”), from Old English force, forca (“forked instrument used to torture”), from Proto-West Germanic *furkō (“fork”), from Latin furca (“pitchfork, forked stake; gallows, beam, stake, support post, yoke”), of uncertain origin. The Middle English word was later reinforced by Anglo-Norman, Old Northern French forque (= Old French forche whence French fourche), also from the Latin. Doublet of fourche and furcate. Cognate also with North Frisian forck (“fork”), D
etymology.native: 「fork」源自中古英語，來自古英語 force，又源自古西日耳曼語 *furkō，再溯自拉丁語 furca，其起源不明。中古英語後受法語影響，亦有盎格魯-諾曼語與古北方法語 forque 的影響。此詞與法語 fourche、furcate 同源，亦與北弗里斯蘭語 forck 相關。

examples.text: Daylight in the room was dwindling.
examples.translation: 房間內的陽光正逐漸減少。

examples.text: Even the longest night gives way to daylight.
examples.translation: 即使最長的黑夜也會迎來白日。

examples.text: I'll smack the living daylights out of you!
examples.translation: 我會把你打得皮開肉綻！

examples.text: There is no night that does not end in daylight.
examples.translation: 沒有哪一夜不會在白日中結束。

examples.text: He had his car stolen in broad daylight.
examples.translation: 他的車子光天化日被偷走了。

examples.text: Today, robbers robbed another bank in broad daylight.
examples.translation: 今天強盜大白天的就搶了另一家銀行。

examples.text: You'll scare the living daylights out of her!
examples.translation: 你會把她嚇得魂飛魄散！

examples.text: Daylight savings is over today.
examples.translation: 今天夏令時結束了。

examples.text: Daylight Savings Time starts on April third.
examples.translation: 夏令時間於四月三日開始。

examples.text: In daylight, Aeneas appears, like a god in countenance and posture.
examples.translation: 在白日裡，阿涅阿斯出現，神態與姿態宛如神明。

examples.text: He wrapt his cloak around him, fell asleep, and dreamed of Lucy Ashton till daylight gleamed through the lattices.
examples.translation: 他將披風裹住自己，睡著了，夢見露西·阿什頓，直到陽光透過窗格灑進來。

examples.text: In those days the entire factory was lit only by daylight and was closed at night.
examples.translation: 在那些日子，整個工廠僅靠白日光線照明，夜晚則關門。

examples.text: We should get home while it's still daylight.
examples.translation: 我們應該趁天還亮時趕回家。

examples.text: We had only two hours to work before daylight.
examples.translation: 我們只有兩個小時的時間在天亮前工作。

examples.text: Budgeting a spy organization can't very well be done in daylight.
examples.translation: 預算間諜組織根本不可能在白天進行。

examples.text: All small running backs instinctively run to daylight.
examples.translation: 所有小型跑衛都本能地朝陽光方向奔去。

examples.text: He could barely see daylight through the complex clockwork.
examples.translation: 他幾乎看不見複雜機械內部透出的白日光線。

examples.text: Finally, after weeks of work on the project, they could see daylight.
examples.translation: 經過數週的專案工作，他們終於看到天光。

examples.text: The minimum and maximum daylights on an injection molding machine determines the sizes of the items it can make.
examples.translation: 注塑機每日的最短與最長光照時間，決定了它能製造的產品尺寸。

etymology.text: From Middle English daye-lighte, dey liȝht, dailiȝt, day-liht, dai-liht (also as days lyȝt, daies liht), equivalent to day + light. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Deegeslucht, Daisljoacht (“daylight”), West Frisian deiljocht (“daylight”), Dutch daglicht (“daylight”), German Tageslicht (“daylight”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 daye-lighte、dey liȝht、dailiȝt、day-liht、dai-liht（亦作 days lyȝt、daies liht），由 day 與 light 組成。與薩特蘭弗里斯蘭語 Deegeslucht、Daisljoacht（「白日光」）、西弗里斯蘭語 deiljocht（「白日光」）、荷蘭語 daglicht（「白日光」）、德語 Tageslicht（「白日光」）同源。

senses.definition: A vessel such as a plate for holding or serving food, often flat with a depressed region in the middle.
The contents of such a vessel.
A specific type of prepared food.
Tableware (including cutlery, etc, as well as crockery) that is to be or is being washed after being used to prepare, serve and eat a meal.
A type of antenna with a similar shape to a plate or bowl.
Something that fits someone's tastes, interests, or abilities.
A sexually attractive person.
The state of being concave, like a dish, or the degree of such concavity.
A hollow place, as in a field.
The home plate.
A trough in which ore is measured.

examples.text: Tom has just finished washing dishes.

examples.text: The Uyghurs' cuisine has all kinds of dishes.

examples.text: Bob was washing the dishes at that time.

examples.text: Every time he comes here, he orders the same dish.
examples.translation: 每次他來這裡點一樣的菜。

examples.text: There was a great variety of dishes on the menu.
examples.translation: 菜單上有各種各樣的菜色。

examples.text: Nothing is so tasty as the dish you make.
examples.translation: 沒有甚麼比你做的菜更好吃了。

examples.text: Can you recommend any vegetarian dishes?

examples.text: A plastic dish will melt on the stove.
examples.translation: 塑膠盤子在烤箱裡會化的。

examples.text: Soon the same waiter came back to pick up the dishes.
examples.translation: 不久，同樣的服務員回來拿起菜。

examples.text: Let’s order the lobster! I’ve heard that’s the specialty dish here.
examples.translation: 讓我們點龍蝦！聽說是這裡的招牌菜。

examples.text: As soon as I came I washed the dishes, so how come you ask me to leave?!
examples.translation: 我一來就在洗碗，你憑什麼叫我走！

examples.text: On busy days like this, I'm glad to have a few dishes I can whip up quickly.
examples.translation: 像今天這樣忙碌的日子，我很慶幸自己能簡單做幾道菜。

examples.text: Neither he nor she wants to do the dishes, and so the two of them decided to eat out.
examples.translation: 他也不想洗碗，她也不想洗碗，所以他們決定出去吃。

examples.text: I haven't had time to do the dishes for two days; they are in a pile in the kitchen sink.
examples.translation: 這兩天我沒時間洗碗，現在廚房的洗碗槽裡已經堆滿了碗碗碟碟。

examples.text: She removed the dishes from the table.
examples.translation: 她把盤子從桌上拿走了。

examples.text: The leek is a versatile vegetable that adds flavor to many dishes.
examples.translation: 蔥是一種多用途的蔬菜，能為許多料理增添風味。

examples.text: In our house, it is customary for everyone to wash his or her own dishes.
examples.translation: 在我家，大家都習慣自己洗自己的盤子。

examples.text: Only the most impeccable dishes are served to the royal family.
examples.translation: 只有最精緻的盤子才會呈獻給皇室家族。

examples.text: The chefs prepared the feast, plating dishes meticulously in the busy kitchen.
examples.translation: 廚師們在忙碌的廚房裡精心擺盤，準備這頓盛宴。

examples.text: Be mindful not to use excessive detergent; it can leave a residue on both your dishes and the dishwasher.
examples.translation: 請勿使用過量洗潔劑，否則會殘留於餐具與洗碗機上。

etymology.text: From Middle English dissh, disch, from Old English disċ (“plate; bowl; dish”), from Proto-West Germanic *disk (“table; dish”) (whence also Proto-Slavic *dъska, whence Bulgarian дъска́ (dăská), Polish deska, Russian доска́ (doská)), Russian чан (čan)) from Latin discus. Doublet of dais, desk, disc, discus, disk, and diskos.
etymology.native: 「dish」源自中古英語 dissh、disch，來自古英語 disċ（意為盤子、碗），源自原始西日耳曼語 *disk（意為桌子、盤子），亦源自拉丁語 discus。此詞與 dais、desk、disc、discus、disk、diskos 為同源詞。

senses.definition: An adult female human.
All female humans collectively; womankind.
A female person, usually an adult: a (generally adult) female sentient being, whether human, supernatural, elf, alien, etc.
A wife (or sometimes a fiancée or girlfriend).
A female person who is extremely fond of or devoted to a specified type of thing. (Used as the last element of a compound.)
A female attendant or servant.

examples.text: Women usually live longer than men.

examples.text: American women didn't have the right to vote.

examples.text: I hate women who say that all men are alike.
examples.translation: 我討厭那些說男人都是一個樣的女人。

examples.text: Generally speaking, women live longer than men.

examples.text: Generally, women live 10 years longer than men.
examples.translation: 女性一般比男性長壽十年。

examples.text: Pregnant women usually buy bigger size panties.
examples.translation: 孕婦一般會買大一號的內褲。

examples.text: Must the woman always play the secondary role?
examples.translation: 女性永遠只能扮演次要角色嗎？

examples.text: Can't you just picture Ed in woman's disguise?

examples.text: Why do women want to sleep in a man's embrace?

examples.text: Oh my god! I've killed a pregnant woman!

examples.text: The young woman was carrying an infant in her arms.
examples.translation: 那個年輕女人手抱著嬰兒。

examples.text: Women's rights groups are going after sexual harassment.

examples.text: Woman as I am, I shall stand up against any social injustice.

examples.text: Pioneer men and women had a hard life, and so did their children.

examples.text: Who's that woman standing over there?
examples.translation: 站在那兒的女人是誰？

examples.text: Who is the woman standing there?
examples.translation: 站在那兒的女人是誰？

etymology.text: From Middle English womman, from earlier wimman, wifman, from Old English wīfmann (“woman”, literally “female person”), a compound of wīf (“woman, female”, whence English wife) + mann (“person, human being”, whence English man). For details on the pronunciation and spelling history, see the usage notes below.
etymology.native: 「woman」源自中世紀英文 womman，更早形式為 wimman 或 wifman，來自古英語 wīfmann（意為「女性人」），由 wīf（意為「女性」，源自英文 wife）與 mann（意為「人」，源自英文 man）組成。關於發音與拼寫演變細節，請參閱下方使用說明。

senses.definition: Bread that has been toasted (cooked lightly by browning).
A proposed salutation (e.g. saying "cheers") while drinking alcohol.
A person, group, or notable object to which a salutation with alcohol is made; a person or group held in similar esteem.
Something that is irreparably damaged or used up, especially when destroyed by heat or fire; something which has been burnt to a crisp or incinerated.
Something that will be no more; something subject to impending destruction, harm or injury.
A type of extemporaneous narrative poem or rap.
An old toast ("a lively fellow who drinks excessively").
A transient, informational pop-up overlay, less interactive than a snackbar.
A piece of toast.

etymology.text: Apparently from an unrecorded Middle English *gust, from Old Norse gustr (“a gust, blast”), from Proto-Germanic *gustiz, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰew-. Cognate with Icelandic gustur (“gust of wind”). Related also to Old Norse gusa (“to gush forth”), Old High German gussa (“flood”), Middle English guschen (> English gush).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語未記載的 *gust，來自古諾斯語 gustr（意為「風暴」），源自原始日耳曼語 *gustiz，再源自原始印歐語 *ǵʰew-。與冰島語 gustur（意為「風暴」）同源，亦與古諾斯語 gusa（意為「噴湧」）、古高地德語 gussa（意為「洪水」）、中古英語 guschen（演變為現代英語 gush）相關。

etymology.text: From Middle English chayere, chayer, chayre, from Old French chaiere, chaere, from Latin cathedra (“seat”), from Ancient Greek καθέδρα (kathédra), from κατά (katá, “down”) + ἕδρα (hédra, “seat”). Partially displaced native stool and settle, which now have more specialised senses. Doublet of cathedra and chaise.

etymology.text: Borrowed from French sofa, ultimately from Arabic صُفَّة (ṣuffa, “a long seat made of stone or brick, covered with rich carpets and cushions and used for sitting”). Cognate with Aramaic צפא/Classical Syriac ܨܦܬܐ (ṣipā’, ṣeppəṯā, “mat, matting”). The word may have entered European languages via Muslim Iberia or through Turkish.
etymology.native: 「sofa」源自法語，最終來自阿拉伯語 صُفَّة (ṣuffa)，意為「用石或磚製成的長椅，鋪有絨毯與靠墊」。此詞亦與阿拉姆語 צפא 及古典敘利亞語 ܨܦܬܐ (ṣipā’, ṣeppəṯā) 同源，意為「墊子」。此詞可能經穆斯林伊比里亞半島或土耳其傳入歐洲語言。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Portuguese banana or Spanish banana, derived from a Niger-Congo language spoken in the Guinea region. Specific derivation is unclear. Possible ancestor or cognate languages include Wolof banaana, Eastern Maninkakan banana, and Vai ꕒꘌꕯ (ɓaana) or ꕒꕌꕯ (ɓaana), possibly from Arabic بَنَان (banān, “fingertip, banana”). However, Ay Baati Wolof (Munro & Gaye, 1997) posits that Wolof banaana is itself derived from Portuguese banana.
etymology.native: 「香蕉」來自葡萄牙語或西班牙語的 banana，源自西非剛果語族中幾內亞地區的語言，具體來源不明。可能的祖先或同源語言包括 Wolof 的 banaana、東部 Maninkakan 的 banana，以及 Vai 的 ꕒꘌꕯ (ɓaana) 或 ꕒꕌꕯ (ɓaana)，可能源自阿拉伯語 بَنَان (banān，意為「指尖、香蕉」)。然而，Ay Baati Wolof（Munro & Gaye, 1997）認為 Wolof 的 banaana 本身源自葡萄牙語的 banana。

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English eg, egg, egge (“egg of a domestic or wild fowl; egg of a snake”) [and other forms] (originally Northern England and Northeast Midlands), from Old Norse egg (“egg”), from Proto-Germanic *ajją (“egg”) (by Holtzmann’s law), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ōwyóm (“egg”), probably from *h₂éwis (“bird”), from *h₂ew- (“to consume”). Doublet of huevo, oeuf, and ovum.
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自中古英語 eg, egg, egge（意為「家禽或野鳥的蛋；蛇的蛋」），來自古諾斯語 egg，再溯源自原始日耳曼語 *ajją（意為「蛋」），由原始印歐語 *h₂ōwyóm 來，可能源自 *h₂éwis（意為「鳥」），而 *h₂ew-（意為「食用」）。是 huevo、oeuf 與 ovum 的同源詞。

Introduced to English and other Western European languages by the Dutch East India Company, who sourced their tea in Amoy; compare Malay teh along the same trade route. etymology.native: 最早出現於1655年左右，源自荷蘭人譯本Álvaro Semedo的著作。來自荷蘭語thee，源自 Hokkien 茶（tê）（同安腔），源自古漢語，最終源自原始漢藏語 *s-la（「葉，茶」）。由荷蘭東印度公司引入英文及其他西歐語言，他們從同安供應茶葉；可與馬來語teh 比較，沿同一貿易路線。與chai及cha為同源詞（且遠源與lahpet之首字同源），詳見相關詞源討論。

etymology.native: 鏡子來自中古英語 mirour，源自古法語 mireor（意為「觀看者」），再源自拉丁語 mīror（意為「驚奇地看」），而拉丁語 mīrus（意為「驚奇的」）則來自印歐語系 *smey-（意為「歡笑、喜悅」）。中古英語原詞 schewere、schawere 亦源自古英語 sċēawere（意為「觀看者」），同時也指「間諜」。

etymology.text: From Middle English rys, from Old French ris, from Old Italian riso, risi, from Byzantine Greek ὄρυζα (óruza), from an Eastern Iranian language related to Middle Persian blnc (*brinǰ), Northern Kurdish riz (beyond Euphrates) and Zazaki riz. Theorized to have come to Iranian languages from Sanskrit व्रीहि (vrīhi).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 rys，來源為古法文 ris，再源自古義大利文 riso、risi，而古拜占庭希臘文 ὄρυζα (óruza) 則來自東伊朗語，與中古波斯文 blnc (*brinǰ)、北庫爾德文 riz（逾底格里斯河）及扎扎基文 riz 有關。學者推測其進入伊朗語系源自梵語 व्रीहि (vrīhi)。

senses.definition: Any of various dishes commonly made by combining liquids, such as water or stock, with other ingredients, such as meat and vegetables, that contribute the food value, flavor, and texture.

senses.definition: A serving of such a dish, typically in a bowl.
The liquid part of such a dish; the broth.
Any mixture or substance suggestive of soup consistency.
Thick fog or cloud (also pea soup).
Nitroglycerine or gelignite, especially when used for safe-cracking.
Dope or cocaine.
Processing chemicals into which film is dipped, such as developer.

etymology.text: The noun is from Middle English soupe, sowpe, from Old French soupe, souppe, sope, from Late Latin suppa (“sopped bread”), from Proto-Germanic *supô (compare Middle Dutch sope (“broth”)). Doublet of sop and zuppa. See also sup and supper.
etymology.native: 這個名詞來自中古英語 soupe、sowpe，源自古法語 soupe、souppe、sope，來源為拉丁語 suppa（意為「泡過的麵包」），再溯自古德語 *supô（可與中世荷蘭語 sope（意為「湯」）相比較）。是 sop 與 zuppa 的同源詞。另見 sup 與 supper。

senses.definition: A flat-bottomed vessel (usually metal) used for cooking food, possibly excluding saucepans (see usage notes).

senses.definition: The nominal household cooking vessel, metaphorically standing for the supply of food for a meal, or for the home.

A vessel used for brewing or serving drinks: a coffee pot or teapot.

A perforated cask for draining sugar.

etymology.text: From Middle English ketel, also chetel, from Old English ċietel (“kettle, cauldron”) and in Middle English possibly influenced by Old Norse ketill and both from Proto-Germanic *katilaz (“kettle, bucket, vessel”), of uncertain origin and formation. Usually regarded as a borrowing of Late Latin catīllus (“small bowl”), diminutive of Latin catinus (“deep bowl, vessel for cooking up or serving food”), however, the word may be Germanic confused with the Latin: compare Old English cete (“cooking pot”)
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 ketel，亦作 chetel，來自古英語 ċietel（「鍋、大鍋」），中古英語時可能受古諾斯語 ketill 影響，皆源自原始日耳曼語 *katilaz（「鍋、桶、容器」），起源與構成不明。通常認為是拉丁語 catīllus（「小碗」）的借詞，此詞為拉丁語 catinus（「深碗、烹煮或盛食之器」）之縮小形，但此詞也可能因德語與拉丁語混淆而產生；可參照古英語 cete（「烹煮鍋」）

etymology.text: From Middle English oven, from Old English ofn (“oven”), from Proto-West Germanic *ofn (“oven”), from Proto-Germanic *uhnaz, *uhwnaz (“oven”). Cognate with West Frisian ûne (“oven”), Dutch oven (“oven”), Low German Aven (“oven”), German Ofen (“oven”), Danish and Norwegian Bokmål ovn (“oven”), Faroese ovnur (“oven”), Icelandic ofn (“oven”), Norwegian Nynorsk omn (“oven”), Swedish ugn (“oven”), Finnish uuni (“oven”), Gothic 𐌰𐌿𐌷𐌽𐍃 (auhns, “oven”)), probably from a Proto-Indo-European *aukʷ- (“cooki
etymology.native: 源自中世英文 oven，來自古英語 ofn（「烤爐」），再溯自原始西日耳曼語 *ofn（「烤爐」），以及原始德語 *uhnaz、*uhwnaz（「烤爐」）。與西弗里斯蘭語 ûne（「烤爐」）、荷蘭語 oven（「烤爐」）、低德語 Aven（「烤爐」）、德語 Ofen（「烤爐」）、丹麥語與挪威語 Bokmål ovn（「烤爐」）、法羅語 ovnur（「烤爐」）、冰島語 ofn（「烤爐」）、挪威語 Nynorsk omn（「烤爐」）、瑞典語 ugn（「烤爐」）、芬蘭語 uuni（「烤爐」）、古高地德語 𐌰𐌿𐌷𐌽𐍃 (auhns,「烤爐」) 同源，可能源自原始印歐語 *aukʷ-（「烤」）

etymology.text: From Middle English towayle, towel, towail, towaille, from Old French toaille (“towel”) (modern French touaille), Medieval Latin toallia, from Frankish *þwahilu (“cloth”), from Proto-Germanic *þwahaną (“to wash”). Cognate with Old High German dwahila (“towel”) (modern dialectal German Zwehle), Dutch dwaal (“towel”), dweil (“mop”), Low German Dweel (“towel”), Old English þwǣle (“band; ribbon; fillet”), Old English þwēan (“to wash”).
etymology.native: 「tow」源自中世紀英格蘭的 towayle，又由古法語 toaille（現代法語 touaille）及中世紀拉丁語 toallia 派生，而古高地德語 dwahila（現代德語 Zwehle）及荷蘭語 dwaal、dweil、低德語 Dweel、古英語 þwǣle 與 þwēan 皆為同源詞，皆與「布」或「洗」有關。

etymology.text: From Middle English pilwe, from Old English pyle, pylu (“pillow”), from Proto-West Germanic *pulwī (“pillow”), from Latin pulvīnus (“cushion”), derived from pulvis (“dust”), for the filler of a pillow. Doublet of pulvinus.

senses.definition: A cart.
A chariot.
A four-wheeled cab, as opposed to a (two-wheeled) Hansom cab.
An unpowered unit in a railroad train, used to hold either passengers or cargo.
A similar vehicle used in special contexts, such as mines, quarries, and mills.
an individual vehicle, powered or unpowered, in a multiple unit.
A passenger-carrying unit in a subway or elevated train, whether powered or not.
A rough unit of quantity approximating the amount which would fill a railroad car.
The moving, load-carrying component of an elevator or other cable-drawn transport mechanism.
The passenger-carrying portion of certain amusement park rides, such as Ferris wheels.

examples.text: What happened? The car's slowing down.

examples.text: I want a compact car with an air conditioner.
examples.translation: 我想要一輛有冷氣的小型車。

examples.text: Watch out for cars when you cross the street.
examples.translation: 當你過馬路的時候要當心汽車。

examples.text: If it rains tomorrow, we will go there by car.
examples.translation: 如果明天下雨，我們就坐車去那兒。

examples.text: Tom advised him not to buy the secondhand car.

examples.text: I want a car, but I have no money to buy one.

examples.text: "Is he by the car?" "No, he is in the car."
examples.translation: 「他在車子旁邊嗎?」 「不, 他在車子裡面。」

examples.translation: 我付他一百美元給我洗車。

examples.text: He was seriously injured in the car accident.
examples.translation: 他在車禍中受了重傷。

examples.text: Car exhaust causes serious pollution in towns.

examples.text: We do not anticipate their buying a new car.
examples.translation: 我們認為他們不會買新車。

examples.text: My brother was injured in the car accident.
examples.translation: 我弟弟在車禍中受了傷。

examples.text: The passing car splashed muddy water on me.
examples.translation: 車子經過的時候把泥水濺到了我的身上。

examples.text: Two men are trying to figure out what's wrong with the car.
examples.translation: 兩個男人在檢查汽車出了什麼故障。

examples.translation: 兩個男人在檢查汽車出了什麼故障。

examples.text: Going to church doesn't make you a Christian any more than standing in a garage makes you a car.
examples.translation: 去教堂參加禮拜，不會馬上就變成一個基督徒，就好像站在車房裡，不會變成一輛車一樣。

examples.text: The locomotive was pulling a long line of freight cars.
examples.translation: 蒸汽機車正拖曳一列長長的貨車。

examples.text: Pollutants like this derive mainly from the combustion of fuel in car engines.
examples.translation: 類似這樣的汙染物主要來自汽車引擎燃燒燃料。

examples.translation: 在車上

examples.text: The conductor coupled the cars to the locomotive.

etymology.text: Inherited from Middle English carre, borrowed from Anglo-Norman carre, from Old Northern French (compare Old French char), from Latin carrus (“two-wheeled baggage wagon”), from Gaulish *karros, from Proto-Celtic *karros (“wagon”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱr̥sós (“vehicle”). Doublet of carrus and horse.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 carre，借自盎格魯-諾曼語 carre，來自古北方法語（與古法語 char 相比），源自拉丁語 carrus（意為「兩輪行李車」），再溯源自高盧語 *karros，來自原始凱爾特語 *karros（意為「車輛」），再溯源自原始印歐語 *ḱr̥sós（意為「車輛」）。是 carrus 與 horse 的同源詞。

Any motorized vehicle, such as a motorbike or car.
An electrical conductor or interface serving as a common connection for two or more circuits or components.

An ambulance.

examples.text: The buses left one after another.
examples.translation: 公車一輛一輛地開出了。

examples.text: You should take the number 5 bus.
examples.translation: 您應該乘5路車。

examples.text: The buses run every ten minutes.
examples.translation: 公車每10分鐘一班。

examples.text: There is a bus every 20 minutes.
examples.translation: 每20分鐘有一班車。

examples.text: How many bus stations are there in this city?
examples.translation: 這座城市有幾個汽車站？

examples.text: Can you tell me where the nearest bus stop is?
examples.translation: 你能把最近的公車站指給我看嗎?

examples.text: What number bus do I take to get to Waikiki?

examples.text: My son always gets sick when he rides a bus.
examples.translation: 我的兒子每次乘坐公車都會暈車。

examples.text: Hurry up, and you will be in time for the bus.
examples.translation: 快點，你就能準時搭上公車了。

examples.text: The bus will take you to the center of the city.
examples.translation: 巴士會把你們帶到市中心。

examples.text: You have to get on that bus to go to the museum.
examples.translation: 要去博物館，你就得乘那輛車。

examples.text: Our restaurant is near the southern bus station.

examples.text: About how long will it take to get there by bus?
examples.translation: 搭公車到那裡大約要花多久的時間？

examples.text: Is this the bus for Park Ridge?

examples.text: The transit passenger expressed anxiety about the delay of the arrival of the bus.

examples.text: There being no vacant seat in the bus, I kept on standing.

etymology.text: Clipping of omnibus. Superseded earlier 'bus, where the apostrophe indicated a clipping. The shift in spelling likely reflects the fact that modern speakers no longer perceive this term as a clipping. The electrical sense is derived from figurative application of the automotive sense.

A male dog, wolf, or fox, as opposed to a bitch or vixen.
The meat of this animal, eaten as food.
A dull, unattractive girl or woman.
A man, guy, chap.

senses.definition: The flesh of this animal eaten as food.
Any similar, chiefly non-domesticated, carnivorous mammal of the family Felidae, which includes bobcats, caracals, cheetahs, cougars, leopards, lions, lynxes, tigers, and other such species.
Chiefly with a descriptive word: an animal not of the family Felidae which (somewhat) resembles a domestic feline (etymology 1, noun sense 1.1.1).
An angry or spiteful person, especially a woman.
An ordinary person, especially a man; a fellow, a guy.
Synonym of itinerant worker.
A jazz musician; also, an enthusiast of jazz music.
Synonym of prostitute.

examples.text: It's raining cats and dogs tonight.

examples.text: The cat will scratch you if you provoke it.
examples.translation: 如果你惹貓，它會抓你。

examples.translation: 如果貓吃掉自己的幼崽，為什麼還會放過老鼠？

examples.text: To say that a cat is instinctively averse to water means that it is the cat's natural reaction towards it.
examples.translation: 說貓天生怕水，意思是它對水有自然的反應。

examples.translation: 斑林狸

etymology.text: From Middle English cat, catte, from Old English catt (“male cat”), catte (“female cat”), from Proto-West Germanic *kattu, from Proto-Germanic *kattuz, generally thought to be from Late Latin cattus (“domestic cat”) (c. 350, Palladius), from Latin catta (c. 75 A.D., Martial), possibly from an Afroasiatic language. Doublet of gato.
etymology.native: 來自中古英語 cat、catte，源自古英語 catt（雄貓）、catte（雌貓），來自原始西日耳曼語 *kattu，再源自原始德語 *kattuz，一般認為來自拉丁語 cattus（家貓，約公元350年，帕拉迪烏斯），源自拉丁語 catta（約公元75年，馬爾提亞利），可能來自阿非羅亞述語系語言。為 gato 的同源詞。

senses.definition: A big cat, Panthera leo, native to Africa, India and formerly much of Europe.
A male lion, as opposed to a lioness, which is characterized by having a flowing shaggy mane and taking little part in hunting, which can be done cooperatively.
Any of various extant and extinct big cats, especially the mountain lion.
A Chinese foo dog.
A person who shows attributes associated with the lion, such as strength, courage, or ferocity.
A famous person regarded with interest and curiosity.
A light brown color that resembles the fur of a lion.
An old Scottish coin, with a lion on the obverse, worth 74 shillings.

etymology.text: From Middle English bird, brid, from Old English bridd (“chick, fledgling, chicken”), of uncertain origin (see Old English bridd for more). Originally from a term used of birds that could not fly (chicks, fledglings, chickens) as opposed to the general Old English term for flying birds, fugol (modern fowl). Gradually replaced fowl as the most common term starting in the 14th century.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 bird, brid，來自古英語 bridd（意為小雞、雛鳥、雞），起源不明（詳見古英語 bridd）。原本用於指無法飛行的鳥類（如雛鳥、小雞），與古英語中泛指飛行鳥類的詞 fugol（現代 fowl）相對。自14世紀起逐漸取代 fowl，成為最常用詞。

senses.definition: To clean thoroughly; to rid of impurities; to cleanse; to clear of (something unwanted).
To remove by cleansing; to wash away.
To free from sin, guilt, or burden.
To evacuate (the bowels or the stomach); to defecate or vomit.
To cause someone to purge; to operate (on somebody) using a cathartic or emetic, or in a similar manner.
To forcibly remove, for example, from political activity.
To forcibly remove people by an organization.
To clear of a charge, suspicion, or imputation.
To clarify; to clear the dregs from (liquor).
To become pure, as by clarification.
To have or produce frequent evacuations from the intestines, as by means of a cathartic.

examples.translation: 無色的綠色意念憤怒地沉睡著。

examples.text: Mountains are not necessarily green.
examples.translation: 山不一定是綠色的。

examples.text: I'm trying to find a green sweater in extra large.
examples.translation: 我正在找一件加大號的綠色毛衣。

examples.translation: 湯姆正努力申請綠卡。

examples.translation: 那個肥肥胖胖、性格兇悍的綠色大魔頭又回來了，準備再開一場動畫冒險。

examples.text: If the moon rises behind the green forest, it looks more like a silver sun that silvers solitude.
examples.translation: 若月亮從綠色森林後升起，它看起來更像一輪銀色太陽，灑下孤寂的銀光。

examples.translation: 利比亞前國旗為全綠色。

relations.native: 容易輕信的、輕信別人的

senses.definition: A foliage leaf or any of the many and often considerably different structures it can specialise into.
Anything resembling the leaf of a plant.
A sheet of a book, magazine, etc. (consisting of two pages, one on each face of the leaf).
A sheet of any substance beaten or rolled until very thin.

Tea leaves.

examples.text: The leaves on the trees fall as winter comes.
examples.translation: 樹上的葉子隨著冬天的到來而掉落。

examples.text: The leaves will turn red in two or three weeks.
examples.translation: 再過兩三週，樹葉就會變紅吧。

examples.text: Autumn came and the leaves started to fall.
examples.translation: 秋天到了，樹葉也開始落下。

examples.text: Meg found a four leaf clover.
examples.translation: 梅格發現了四片葉子的三葉草。

examples.text: The leaves on the trees rustle gently in the wind.
examples.translation: 樹葉在風中簌簌作響。

examples.text: The leaves rustle in the wind.
examples.translation: 樹葉在風中簌簌作響。

examples.text: When it's windy, the leaves of the old oak rustle and its branches creak.
examples.translation: 刮風的時候，老橡樹的葉子會沙沙作響，樹枝會發出嘎吱聲。

examples.text: When the wind blows, the leaves of the old oak rustle, and the branches creak.
examples.translation: 刮風的時候，老橡樹的葉子會沙沙作響，樹枝會發出嘎吱聲。

examples.text: She was a rickety girl, like a yellowish leaf that can't do photosynthesis.
examples.translation: 她像一片黃色的枯葉，無法進行光合作用。

examples.text: The train car has one single-leaf and two double-leaf doors per side.
examples.translation: 列車車廂每側設有一扇單葉門和兩扇雙葉門。

etymology.text: From Middle English lef, leef, from Old English lēaf, from Proto-West Germanic *laub, from Proto-Germanic *laubą (“leaf”), from Proto-Indo-European *lowbʰ-o-m, from *lewbʰ- (“to cut off”).
etymology.native: 來源於中世紀英文 lef、leef，源自古英語 lēaf，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *laub，源自古德語 *laubą（意為「葉子」），再溯自印歐語系 *lowbʰ-o-m，源自 *lewbʰ-（意為「割下」）

Containing much foliage.
In the form of leaves (of some material).

examples.text: Algiers needs more beautiful and leafy trees.
examples.translation: Algiers 需要更多美麗且蔥鬱的樹木。

examples.translation: 這片蔥鬱的社區裡有很多林蔭大道。

examples.text: Try to eat more leafy green vegetables.
examples.translation: 試著多吃一些綠葉蔬菜。

examples.translation: 我驚訝地發現，有人真的不吃綠葉蔬菜。

examples.translation: 那隻鹿只吃灌木的蔥鬱頂端，不啃枝幹。

examples.text: "Well?" I inquired, as soon as we were protected from prying eyes by the leafy screen.
examples.translation: 「怎麼樣？」我問，一當我們被蔥鬱的屏風掩護，免遭他人偷看。

examples.text: a leafy avenue
examples.translation: 一條蔥鬱的大道

examples.text: They live in a beautiful house in a leafy suburb.
examples.translation: 他們住在一個位於蔥鬱郊區的漂亮房舍裡。

examples.translation: 這棵樹的樹頂蔥鬱茂密。

examples.text: New York bristles with towering buildings.
examples.translation: 紐約充滿著高樓大廈。

examples.text: This building is LEED Platinum certified.
examples.translation: 該建築已獲 LEED 白金認證。

examples.text: Special forces surrounded the building.
examples.translation: 特種部隊包圍了建築物。

examples.text: The building is seven stories high.
examples.translation: 這棟建築物有七層樓高。

examples.text: The soldiers occupied the building.
examples.translation: 士兵們佔領了這個建築。

examples.text: I wonder when this building was constructed.
examples.translation: 我很好奇那個建築物是什麼時候建造的。

examples.text: Please let me off in front of that building.
examples.translation: 請讓我在那棟房子前下車。

examples.text: The high building can be seen from the window.
examples.translation: 從窗戶可以看見高樓。

examples.text: There are daisies next to the steel building.
examples.translation: 在鋼鐵大廈的旁邊有許多的雛菊。

examples.text: A new school building is under construction.
examples.translation: 一座新的教學樓正在建設。

examples.text: There are daisies around the steel building.
examples.translation: 那裡有許多雛菊圍繞著鋼鐵大廈。

examples.text: Kids are building sand castles on the beach.
examples.translation: 孩子們正在海灘上用沙子堆沙堡。

examples.text: The building was divided into four rooms.
examples.translation: 這棟建築物分成四個房間。

examples.text: Formerly this building was a hospital.
examples.translation: 這幢樓以前是醫院。

examples.text: This building is near completion.
examples.translation: 這座建築物快完工了。

examples.text: The expansion of the building's west end is being studied.
examples.translation: 西面大樓的擴建在研究中。

examples.text: We are building your house in compliance with your wishes.
examples.translation: 我們依照您的願望為您建造房屋。

examples.text: The two buildings adjoin.
examples.translation: 這兩棟建築相鄰。

examples.text: Look at that building standing on the hill.
examples.translation: 看那座山頂上的建築。

examples.text: Tom was standing just in front of a large building that was up for sale.
examples.translation: 湯姆站在一座大樓前，那棟樓正待出售。

etymology.text: From Middle English byldynge, buyldyng, byldyng, buldynge, buldyng, boldyng, equivalent to build + -ing. Compare also related Middle English bold (“edifice, castle, mansion”), from Old English bold (“building, dwelling, house”).

examples.text: All the students clapped their hands.
examples.translation: 所有的學生都拍手。

examples.text: Tom's hands are stronger than mine.
examples.translation: 湯姆的雙手比我的強壯。

examples.text: Wash your hands before each meal.
examples.translation: 飯前洗手

examples.text: She greeted him waving her hand.
examples.translation: 她揮著手向他打招呼。

examples.text: You haven't washed your hands yet, have you?
examples.translation: 你還沒洗手，不是嗎？

examples.text: I entered the room and shook hands with him.
examples.translation: 我走進了房間與他握手。

examples.text: My right hand is Uighur, and my left is Han.
examples.translation: 我的右手是維族的，左手是漢族的。

examples.text: She was holding a small parasol in her hand.
examples.translation: 她手裡握著一把小陽傘。

examples.text: The young man put out his hand and I shook it.
examples.translation: 年輕人伸出他的手，接著我和他握了手。

examples.text: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
examples.translation: 一鳥在手勝過二鳥在林。

examples.text: Those homeless people are living hand-to-mouth.
examples.translation: 那些無家可歸的人每天過著僅夠糊口的生活。

examples.text: She waved her hand to me, smiling brightly.
examples.translation: 她笑眯眯的對我招手。

examples.text: Theory and practice should go hand in hand.
examples.translation: 理論得聯絡實際。

examples.text: Never rub your eyes when your hands are dirty.
examples.translation: 手髒的時候千萬不要揉眼睛。

examples.text: He put his hand gently on her shoulder.
examples.translation: 他把他的手溫柔地放在她的肩上。

examples.text: My hands were shaking too much to thread the needle.
examples.translation: 我的手抖得太厲害，沒法穿針了。

examples.text: Never rub your eyes with dirty hands.
examples.translation: 手髒的時候千萬不要揉眼睛。

examples.text: What I have in my hand is a fossil seashell.
examples.translation: 在我手裡的是一個貝殼化石。

examples.text: She held a large bouquet of artificial flowers in her hands.
examples.translation: 她手裡拿著一大束假花。

examples.text: My right hand is numb.
examples.translation: 我的右手麻了。

examples.text: The market on the promenade sells second-hand clothes and bric-a-brac.
examples.translation: 海濱市場賣二手衣物和小雜貨。

examples.text: The bout turned out rough and neither boxer was going to win hands down.
examples.translation: 這場比賽結果很激烈，兩位拳手都沒人能毫無爭議地獲勝。

examples.text: He kept trying to see my hand.
examples.translation: 他一直試圖看我的手。

senses.definition: With a descriptive word: the part of the sky which can be seen from a specific place or at a specific time; its climate, condition, etc.
Usually preceded by the: the abode of God or the gods, angels, the souls of deceased people, etc.; heaven; also, powers emanating from heaven.
The set of all lightlike lines (or directions) passing through a given point in space-time.
In an art gallery: the upper rows of pictures that cannot easily be seen; also, the place where such pictures are hung.
A cloud.

examples.text: The sky was filled with aeroplanes.
examples.translation: 天上滿是飛機。

examples.text: The sky was ablaze with fireworks.
examples.translation: 天空被焰火點亮。

examples.text: The sky became darker and darker.
examples.translation: 天空變得越來越暗了。

examples.text: The clouds floating in the sky are beautiful.
examples.translation: 天空飄的雲很美。

examples.text: Not a single cloud could be seen in the sky.
examples.translation: 天上萬里無雲。

examples.text: Do you know the reason why the sky looks blue?
examples.translation: 你知道為什麼天看起來這麼藍嗎？

examples.text: At dusk, the sky was dyed with purple light.
examples.translation: 黃昏時分，天空染上了紫色的光。

examples.text: Countless stars were twinkling in the sky.
examples.translation: 無數星星在天上閃爍。

examples.text: There is a mass of dark clouds in the sky.
examples.translation: 空中有一大片烏雲。

examples.text: The sky today is the bluest that I've ever seen it.
examples.translation: 今天的天空是我看過最藍的天空。

examples.text: Suddenly, the clouds darkened the sky.
examples.translation: 天空突然變得烏雲密佈。

examples.text: A cloud is a mass of vapor in the sky.
examples.translation: 雲是天空中的水汽團。

examples.text: A sharp crack of thunder split the sky.
examples.translation: 一道閃電劃破天空。

examples.text: A cloud of dust and debris rose and lingered in the sky for a few minutes afterward.
examples.translation: 一團塵土與瓦礫騰空而起，在空中盤旋了數分鐘。

examples.text: When I was little, I often lay on the grass and watched the white clouds in the sky.
examples.translation: 我小時候常常躺在草地上看天上的白雲。

examples.text: The most beautiful thing in the sky are the stars, the most beautiful thing in life is kindness.
examples.translation: 天上最美是星星，人生最美是溫情。

examples.text: A few faint stars were gleaming in the violet sky.
examples.translation: 幾顆微弱的星星在紫羅蘭色的天空閃耀。

examples.text: He went on a quest to find the point where the sky touches the Earth.
examples.translation: 他踏上尋找天與地相接之處的旅程。

examples.text: The stars shine in the profound sky, enlightening the hearts of the world.
examples.translation: 星辰在深邃的天空閃耀，照亮了世界的心靈。

examples.text: To the west a dark church spire rose up against a marigold sky.
examples.translation: 西方一座暗色教堂尖塔聳立於萬壽菊色的天空下。

examples.text: The mountain is standing out in sharp relief against the blue sky.
examples.translation: 山巒在藍天背景下顯得格外清晰銳利。

examples.text: Dragons flew in the sky, raining down fiery death and destruction on the hapless villagers.
examples.translation: 龍在天空飛翔，將熾熱的死亡與毀滅傾瀉在無辜的村民身上。

etymology.text: The noun is derived from Middle English sky (“sky; cloud; mist”), also spelled ski, skie, [and other forms], from Old Norse ský (“cloud”), from Proto-Germanic *skiwją (“cloud; sky”), from *skiwô (“cloud; cloud cover, haze; sky”) (whence Old English sċēo (“cloud”) and Middle English skew (“air; sky; (rare) cloud”)), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewH- (“to cover; to conceal, hide”).
etymology.native: 這個名詞源自中古英語 sky（天空、雲霧），也寫作 ski、skie 等，來自古諾斯語 ský（雲），再溯源自原始日耳曼語 *skiwją（雲、天空），來自 *skiwô（雲、霧氣、天空），進而影響古英語 sċēo 與中古英語 skew（空氣、天空、罕見的雲）；而這些詞根又來自原始印歐語 *(s)kewH-（覆蓋、隱藏）

etymology.text: From Middle English wal, from Old English weall (“wall, dike, earthwork, rampart, dam, rocky shore, cliff”), from Proto-West Germanic *wall (“wall, rampart, entrenchment”), from Latin vallum (“wall, rampart, entrenchment, palisade”), from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind, roll”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 wal，來自古英語 weall（意為「牆、堤壩、土壩、防禦工事、水壩、岩岸、峭壁」），源自古西日耳曼語 *wall（意為「牆、防禦工事、壕溝」），源自拉丁語 vallum（意為「牆、防禦工蹟、木柵欄」），源自印歐語系原始詞 *welH-（意為「轉動、旋轉、滾動」）

etymology.text: From Middle English label (“narrow band, strip of cloth”), from Old French label, lambel (Modern French lambeau), from Frankish *lappā (“torn piece of cloth”), from Proto-Germanic *lappǭ, *lappô (“cloth stuff, rag, scraps, flap, dewlap, lobe, rabbit ear”), from Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“blade”). Cognate with Old High German lappa (“rag, piece of cloth”), Old English læppa (“skirt, flap of a garment”). More at lap.
etymology.native: 「label」源自中世英文，意為「窄帶、布條」，來源於古法文 label、lambel（現代法文 lambeau），再溯源自古弗蘭克語 *lappā（意為「撕裂的布片」），而古德語 *lappǭ、*lappô（意為「布料、碎布、翻邊、下垂的皮毛、耳廓」），源自印歐語系 *leb-（意為「刀片」）。與古高地德語 lappa（意為「布頭、布片」）、古英語 læppa（意為「裙襬、衣物的翻邊」）同源。詳見 lap。

etymology.text: From Middle English fom, foom, from Old English fām, from Proto-West Germanic *faim, from Proto-Germanic *faimaz, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)poHy-m-os, from *(s)poH(y)- (“foam”). Cognate with German Feim (“foam”), Latin spūma (“foam”), Latin pūmex (“pumice”), Sanskrit फेन (phéna, “foam”), possibly Northern Kurdish fê (“epilepsy”).

etymology.text: From Middle English overschadwen, overschadewe, from Old English ofersċeadwian (“to overshadow”), equivalent to over- + shadow. Compare with West Frisian oerskaduwe (“to overshadow”), Dutch overschaduwen (“to overshadow”), German überschatten (“to overshadow”), Gothic 𐌿𐍆𐌰𐍂𐍃𐌺𐌰𐌳𐍅𐌾𐌰𐌽 (ufarskadwjan, “to overshadow”), and more distantly, Old Norse yfirskyggja (“to overshadow”), Danish overskygge (“to overshadow”), Swedish överskugga (“to overshadow”), Old English ofersċūwan (“to overshadow”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 overschadwen、overschadewe，來自古英語 ofersċeadwian（意為「遮蔽」），由 over- + shadow 組成。可與西弗里斯蘭語 oerskaduwe（意為「遮蔽」）、荷蘭語 overschaduwen（意為「遮蔽」）、德語 überschatten（意為「遮蔽」）、古高地德語 𐌿𐍆𐌰𐍂𐍃𐌺𐌰𐌳𐍅𐌾𐌰𐌽（ufarskadwjan，意為「遮蔽」）相對應，更遠古的則有古諾斯語 yfirskyggja（意為「遮蔽」）、丹麥語 overskygge（意為「遮蔽」）、瑞典語 överskugga（意為「遮蔽」），以及古英語 ofersċūwan（意為「遮蔽」）。

etymology.text: First attested in 1425–1475, in Middle English; from Middle English illiterat(e) (“uneducated, ignorant of Latin”), borrowed from Latin illīterātus, illitterātus (“unlearned, ignorant”), itself from in- (“un-”) + līterātus, litterātus (“furnished with letters”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from lītera, littera (“letter, character”). The noun was derived from the adjective by substantivization, see -ate (noun-forming suffix).
etymology.native: 最早見於1425–1475年間的中古英語，源自中古英語illiterat(e)（意為「未受過教育、不懂拉丁文」），借自拉丁語illīterātus、illitterātus（意為「未受過教育、不懂書寫」），本身由in-（意為「非」）+ līterātus、litterātus（意為「有字母、有文字」）構成（見-ate（形容詞構成後綴）），而lītera、littera（意為「字母、字形」）則源自拉丁語。此名詞由形容詞衍生，透過名詞化構成（見-ate（名詞構成後綴））。

etymology.text: Origin uncertain, but probably from a frequentative form of Middle English *cudden, cuththen, keththen (“to embrace”), a variant of cuthen, kuthen, kithen (“to be familiar with, make known”), from Middle English cuth, couth (“known, familiar”), equivalent to couth + -le. Cognate with Middle Dutch kudden (“to come together, flock together”). More at couth.
etymology.native: 起源不明，但可能來自中古英語 *cudden, cuththen, keththen（意為「擁抱」），為 cuthen, kuthen, kithen（意為「熟悉、告知」）的變體，源自中古英語 cuth, couth（意為「熟知、熟悉」），等同於 couth + -le。與中古荷蘭語 kudden（意為「聚集、群聚」）同源。詳見 couth。

senses.definition: An article of clothing worn over the front of the torso and/or legs for protection from spills; also historically worn by Freemasons and as part of women's fashion.
The short cassock ordinarily worn by English bishops.
The paved area of an airport, especially the area where aircraft park away from a terminal.
The spreading end of a driveway.
The paved area below the yellow line on a racetrack.
The loading, parking or roadway area immediately beside a railway station or marine terminal.
The portion of a stage extending towards the audience beyond the proscenium arch in a theatre.
A large decal toward the bottom of a pinball table.
A raised panel below a window or wall monument or tablet.
The sides of a tree's canopy.
The cap of a cannon; a piece of lead laid over the vent to keep the priming dry.

etymology.text: Rebracketing of napron (a napron → an apron), from Middle English naperoun, napron, apron, from Old French napperon, diminutive of nappe (“tablecloth”), from Latin mappa (“napkin”). For other similar cases of rebracketing, see adder, daffodil, newt, nickname, orange, trickle, umpire.
etymology.native: 「napron」的語源來自中古英語 naperoun、napron，意為「圍裙」，源自法語 napperon，是「nappe（桌布）」的縮小形，再源自拉丁語 mappa（餐巾）。其他類似語詞如 adder、daffodil、newt、nickname、orange、trickle、umpire 也有類似語源轉移現象。

etymology.text: From Middle English eri (“fearful”), from Old English earg (“cowardly, fearful”), from Proto-West Germanic *arg, from Proto-Germanic *argaz. Akin to Scots ergh, argh from the same Old English source. Doublet of argh.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 eri（意為「害怕」），來自古英語 earg（意為「膽怯、害怕」），源自原始西日耳曼語 *arg，再源自原始日耳曼語 *argaz。與蘇格蘭語 ergh、argh 來自相同古英語源。為 argh 的同義詞。

senses.definition: Eerie, or suggestive of ghosts or the supernatural.
Spooked; afraid; frightened.
Unpredictably excitable; skittish (used especially of horses).

etymology.text: From spook + -y.

senses.definition: Striving; earnest endeavor; hard work.
Exertion or contention for superiority, either by physical or intellectual means.
Bitter conflict, sometimes violent.
A trouble of any kind.
That which is contended against; occasion of contest.

etymology.text: From Middle English strif, stryf, striffe, from Old French estrif, noun derived from estriver, from Frankish *strīban; compare Dutch strijven. More at strive.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 strif、stryf、striffe，來自古法文 estrif，為由 estriver 派生之名詞，源自古弗蘭克語 *strīban；可參見 Dutch strijven。

senses.definition: Any small, natural and bright dot in the sky, most visible in the night or twilight sky. This sense includes the planets, but it is now sometimes used in exclusion of them due to influence from the technical astronomical sense.
A planet thought to influence one's fate; (figuratively) fate or luck.
A very massive ball of plasma with strong enough gravity to have ongoing fusion of hydrogen or heavier elements in its core. In strict technical usage, the Sun is included.
An asterisk (*) or comparable symbol (e.g., ★, ☆, ✶, ✦, ✧, ✷, ✪, ⭐) inspired by a celestial star.
A network topology with multiple computers individually merging to one central switch, thus free of risk of collisions. A single point of failure can occur if the switch experiences corruption.

A simple dance, or part of a dance, where a group of four dancers each put their right or left hand in the middle and turn around in a circle. You call them right-hand stars or left-hand stars, depending on the hand which is in the middle.
A star-shaped ornament worn on the breast to indicate rank or honour in a military. Now often used metonymically for military rankings.
A symbol used to rate hotels, films, etc. with a higher number of stars denoting better quality.
An actor in a leading role.
An exceptionally talented or famous person, often in a specific field; a celebrity.

etymology.text: From Middle English sterre, from Old English steorra (“star”), from Proto-West Germanic *sterrō, variant of *sternō, from Proto-Germanic *sternô, *sternǭ (“star”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂stḗr (“star”). Doublet of aster; related to estoile, étoile, stella, and stelo.
etymology.native: 「star」源自中古英語 sterre，來源為古英語 steorra，再溯自古西日耳曼語 *sterrō，為 *sternō 的變體，而 *sternō 又源自古德語 *sternô、*sternǭ，最終來自印歐語系 *h₂stḗr。「star」與 aster、estoile、étoile、stella、stelo 等詞相關。

senses.definition: To set free, release or discharge (from obligations, debts, responsibility etc.).
To resolve; to explain; to solve.
To pronounce free from or give absolution for a penalty, blame, or guilt.
To pronounce not guilty; to grant a pardon for.
To grant a remission of sin; to give absolution to.
To remit a sin; to give absolution for a sin.
To finish; to accomplish.
To pass a course or test; to gain credit for a class; to qualify academically.

etymology.text: Learned borrowing from Latin nebula (“little cloud, mist”). First attested in 1655. Akin to Ancient Greek νεφέλη (nephélē, “cloud”), German Nebel (“mist, nebula”), Old Norse nifl, Polish niebo (“sky, heaven”), Russian не́бо (nébo, “sky”).
etymology.native: 從拉丁語 nebula（「小雲、霧」）借入，最早見於1655年。與古希臘語 νεφέλη（nephélē，「雲」）、德語 Nebel（「霧、星雲」）、古挪威語 nifl、波蘭語 niebo（「天空、天堂」）、俄語 не́бо（nébo，「天空」）相關。

senses.definition: The Milky Way; the apparent band of concentrated stars which appears in the night sky over earth.
Any of the collections of many millions or billions of stars, galactic dust, black holes, etc. existing as independent and coherent systems, of which there are billions in the known universe.
An assemblage of things or people seen as luminous or brilliant.
Any print or pattern reminiscent of a galaxy, generally consisting of blending, semiopaque patches of vibrant color on a dark background.

pronunciations.value: G AE1 L AH0 K S IY0

examples.text: Soon, the expanse of the galaxy became reminiscent of ancient Polynesian migrational waves throughout the Pacific Ocean.

examples.text: ‘extragalactic nebula’ is a former name for ‘galaxy’.
examples.translation: 「外星系星雲」曾是「星系」的舊稱。

etymology.text: From Middle English galaxye, galaxie, from Old French galaxie, from Latin galaxias, from Ancient Greek γαλαξίας (galaxías, “Milky Way”), shortening of γαλαξίας κύκλος (galaxías kúklos, “milky circle”), from γάλα (gála, “milk”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 galaxye，galaxie，來自古法文 galaxie，源自拉丁文 galaxias，來自古希臘文 γαλαξίας（galaxías，「銀河」），是 γαλαξίας κύκλος（galaxías kúklos，「銀河圈」）的縮寫，而 γάλα（gála，「牛奶」）是其語源。

senses.definition: An elliptical movement of an object about a celestial object or Lagrange point, especially a periodic elliptical revolution.
One complete circuit round an orbited body.
The state of moving in an orbit.
The path of an electron around an atomic nucleus.
A path for the ball on the outer edge of the playfield, usually connected so that the ball entering in one end will come out of the other.
A sphere of influence; an area or extent of activity, interest, or control.
The bony cavity in the skull of a vertebrate containing the eyeball.
The area around the eye of a bird or other animal.
A collection of points related by the evolution function of a dynamical system.
The subset of elements of a set X to which a given element can be moved by members of a specified group of transformations that act on X.
senses.native: 變換群作用下可達元素集合

senses.definition: The number of hands such that each player at the table has posted the big blind once.

etymology.text: From Middle English thudden (“to strike with a weapon”), from Old English þyddan (“to strike, press, thrust”), from Proto-Germanic *þuddijaną, *þiudijaną (“to strike, thrust”), from Proto-Germanic *þūhaną, *þeuhaną (“to press”), from Proto-Indo-European *tūk- (“to beat”). Cognate with Old English þoddettan (“to strike, push, batter”), Old English þȳdan (“to strike, stab, thrust, press”), Old English þēowan (“to press”), Albanian thundër (“a hoof, talon, a shaft", figuratively, "oppression, torme
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 thudden（意為「以武器擊打」），來自古英語 þyddan（意為「擊打、壓迫、刺入」），源自原始日耳曼語 *þuddijaną、*þiudijaną（意為「擊打、刺入」），再溯源自原始日耳曼語 *þūhaną、*þeuhaną（意為「壓迫」），更上溯至原始印歐語 *tūk-（意為「敲打」）。與古英語 þoddettan（意為「擊打、推擠、猛擊」）、þȳdan（意為「擊打、刺入、壓迫」）、þēowan（意為「壓迫」），以及阿爾巴尼亞語 thundër（意為「蹄、爪、杆」，比喻「壓迫、暴政」）同源。

etymology.text: From Middle English lynnen, lynen, from Old English līnen (“linen", "made of flax”), from Proto-West Germanic *līnīn (“made of flax”), from Proto-Germanic *līną (“flax”), from Proto-Indo-European *līno- (“flax”), equivalent to line + -en. Cognate with Latin līnum (“flax”) and thus also Linum. More at line.
etymology.native: 「linen」源自中世英文 lynnen、lynen，來源於古英文 līnen（意為「亞麻製品」），再溯源自古西日耳曼語 *līnīn（意為「亞麻製品」），更上溯至古德語 *līną（意為「亞麻」），再往上溯至印歐語系 *līno-（意為「亞麻」），與拉丁文 līnum（亞麻）同源，亦與 Linum 有關。詳見 line。

Displaced native Old English stōw, stede (partially), and -ern. Compare also English pleck (“plot of ground”), West Frisian plak (“plac
etymology.native: 「place」源自中古英語，融合古英語 plæċe（意為「地方、開闊空間、街道」）與古法語 place（意為「廣場、開闊空間」），二者皆源自拉丁語 platēa（意為「廣場、寬闊街道」），再溯源自古希臘語 πλατεῖα（plateîa），為 πλατεῖα ὁδός（plateîa hodós，意為「寬闊道路」）之縮寫，而古希臘語則源自原始印歐語 *pleth₂-（意為「延展」），其由 *pleh₂-（意為「平坦」）延伸而來。此詞取代了古英語 stōw 與 stede（部分）之用法。亦可參見英文 pleck（意為「一塊土地」）與西弗里斯蘭語 plak（意為「廣場」）

Norrice and nourrice are derived from Late Latin nūtrīcia (“wet nurse”), from Latin nūtrīcius (“that nurses or suckles; nourishing”), from nūtriō (“to breastfeed, nurse, suckle”), possibly ultimat
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 noricerie、norserye（意為「孩童育養之地；被撫養或哺乳的狀態；教育、育養」），來自古法文 norricerie、nourricerie，源自 norrice、nourrice（現代法文 nourrice，意為「育兒保姆、哺乳母」）＋-erie（構成女性名詞的後綴）。norrice 與 nourrice 來自拉丁文 nūtrīcia（意為「哺乳母」），源自拉丁文 nūtrīcius（意為「哺乳或餵養者；餵養之物」），來自 nūtriō（意為「哺乳、餵養」），可能源自最古老的詞源。

etymology.text: From Middle English wowen, woȝen, from Old English wōgian (“to woo, court, marry”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Scots wow (“to woo”). Perhaps related to Old English wōg, wōh (“bending, crookedness”), in the specific sense of "bend or incline (some)one toward oneself". If so, then derived from Proto-Germanic *wanhō (“a bend, angle”), from Proto-Indo-European *wonk- (“crooked, bent”), from Proto-Indo-European *wā- (“to bend, twist, turn”); related to Old Norse vá (“corner, angle”).
etymology.native: 此詞源自中古英語 wowen, woȝen，來自古英語 wōgian（意為「追求、迎娶」），起源不明。與蘇格蘭語 wow（意為「追求」）同源。可能與古英語 wōg, wōh（意為「彎曲、曲折」）有關，特指「使某人傾向於自己」。若如此，則源自原始日耳曼語 *wanhō（意為「彎曲、角度」），再源自原始印歐語 *wonk-（意為「彎曲、彎折」），而原始印歐語 *wā-（意為「彎曲、扭轉、轉向」）；亦與古諾斯語 vá（意為「角落、角度」）相關。

etymology.text: From Middle English bischop, bishop, bisshop, biscop, from Old English bisċop (“bishop”), from Proto-West Germanic *biskop, from Vulgar Latin (e)biscopus, from classical Latin episcopus (“overseer, supervisor”), from Ancient Greek ἐπίσκοπος (epískopos, “overseer”), from ἐπί (epí, “over”) + σκοπός (skopós, “watcher”), used in Greek and Latin both generally and as a title of civil officers. Cognate with all European terms for the position in various Christian churches; compare also Middle English
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 bischop、bishop、bisshop、biscop，來自古英語 bisċop（主教），源自古西日耳曼語 *biskop，來自通俗拉丁語（e）biscopus，來自古典拉丁語 episcopus（監督者），源自古希臘語 ἐπίσκοπος（epískopos，監督者），由 ἐπί（epí，「在上」）+ σκοπός（skopós，「監視者」）組成，希臘語與拉丁語中皆用作一般職稱或官職名稱。與歐洲各基督教教會中所有「主教」職稱同源；亦可參見中古英語「」。

etymology.text: Shortened from gooney, from obsolete gony (“simpleton”), used circa 1580, of unknown origin. Perhaps a familiar term derived from Middle English gone, a variant of gome (“man, person”). Gony was applied by sailors to the albatross and similar big, clumsy birds (circa 1839). The term goon first carried the meaning "stupid person" (circa 1921). Compare Scots goni, guni (“a bogey, bugbear, hobgoblin”), dialectal Swedish gonnar (“elves, goblins”, plural).
etymology.native: 「gooney」源自已廢棄的「gony」（意為「傻瓜」），約在1580年使用，起源不明。可能源自中古英格蘭的「gone」，為「gome」（意為「人」）的變體。 sailors 約在1839年用「gony」形容鴨嘴鳥等笨重的大鳥。直到1921年，「goon」才開始指「愚蠢的人」。可與蘇格蘭語「goni」、「guni」（意為「惡魔、妖怪」）及瑞典方言「gonnar」（意為「精靈、小妖」）相對照。

etymology.text: From Middle English happy (“fortunate, happy”), perhaps an alteration of Middle English happyn, happen (“fortunate, happy”), possibly related to or from Old Norse heppinn (“fortunate, happy”); and potentially assimilated to be equivalent to hap (“chance, luck, fortune”) + -y. Compare also Icelandic heppinn (“lucky”), Faroese heppin (“fortunate, lucky, happy”), Norwegian Nynorsk heppen (“lucky”), Scots happin (“fortunate, blessed”). See further at hap.
etymology.native: 「happy」源自中古英語 hapyn 或 happen，意為「幸運、幸福」，可能與古諾斯語 heppinn（意為「幸運」）有關；也可能與 hap（意為「機會、運氣」）+ -y 結合而成。可參照冰島語 heppinn（意為「幸運」）、法羅語 heppin（意為「幸運、幸福」）、挪威語 Nynorsk heppen（意為「幸運」）及蘇格蘭語 happin（意為「幸運、祝福」）。詳見 hap。

etymology.text: From Middle English bred, breed, from Old English brēad (“fragment, bit, morsel, crumb", also "bread”), from Proto-West Germanic *braud, from Proto-Germanic *braudą (“bread”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerw-, *bʰrewh₁- (“to boil; to brew”), from *bʰer- (“to bear, carry”). Alternatively, from Proto-Germanic *braudaz, *brauþaz (“broken piece, fragment”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰera- (“to split, beat, hew, struggle”) (see brittle). Perhaps a conflation of the two. Possibly a doublet of broa.
etymology.native: 「bread」源自中世英文的 bred、breed，來自古英文 brēad（意為「碎片、小塊、碎屑」，亦指「麵包」），再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *braud，來自原始日耳曼語 *braudą（意為「麵包」），再往上溯源自原始印歐語 *bʰerw-、*bʰrewh₁-（意為「煮沸、發酵」），而 *bʰer-（意為「承載、攜帶」）。另一說法源自原始日耳曼語 *braudaz、*brauþaz（意為「破碎的片段」），來自原始印歐語 *bʰera-（意為「劈開、敲打、切割」）（見 brittle）。可能為兩者融合而成，也可能為 broa 的同源詞。

etymology.text: Borrowed from Portuguese banana or Spanish banana, derived from a Niger-Congo language spoken in the Guinea region. Specific derivation is unclear. etymology.text: First appears c. 1655, in the English translation Álvaro Semedo’s writings. From Dutch thee, from Hokkien 茶 (tê) (Amoy dialect), from Old Chinese, ultimately from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *s-la (「leaf, tea」). Introduced to English and other Western European languages by the Dutch East India Company, who sourced their tea in Amoy; compare Malay teh along the same trade route. Doublet of chai and cha (and, distantly, the first element of lahpet), from same Proto-Sino-Tibetan root; see discussion of cogn
etymology.native: 最早出現於1655年左右，源自荷蘭人譯本Álvaro Semedo的著作。來自荷蘭語thee，源自 Hokkien 茶（tê）（同安腔），源自古漢語，最終源自原始漢藏語 *s-la（「葉，茶」）。由荷蘭東印度公司引入英文及其他西歐語言，他們從同安供應茶葉；可與馬來語teh 比較，沿同一貿易路線。與chai及cha為同源詞（且遠源與lahpet之首字同源），詳見相關詞源討論。

etymology.text: First attested in 1425–1475, in Middle English; from Middle English illiterat(e) (“uneducated, ignorant of Latin”), borrowed from Latin illīterātus, illitterātus (“unlearned, ignorant”), itself from in- (“un-”) + līterātus, litterātus (“furnished with letters”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), from lītera, littera (“letter, character”). The noun was derived from the adjective by substantivization, see -ate (noun-forming suffix).
etymology.native: 最早見於1425–1475年間的中古英語，源自中古英語illiterat(e)（意為「未受過教育、不懂拉丁文」），借自拉丁語illīterātus、illitterātus（意為「未受過教育、不懂書寫」），本身由in-（意為「非」）+ līterātus、litterātus（意為「有字母、有文字」）構成（見-ate（形容詞構成後綴）），而lītera、littera（意為「字母、字形」）則源自拉丁語。此名詞由形容詞衍生，透過名詞化構成（見-ate（名詞構成後綴））。

senses.definition: An intimate physical embrace, typically while lying (or sitting): a snuggle, an instance of lying together snugly, as one might with a partner (more intimate than a hug, and typically of longer duration).

Cognate with Middle Dutch kudden (“to come together, flock together”). More at couth.
etymology.native: 起源不明，但可能來自中古英語 *cudden, cuththen, keththen（意為「擁抱」），為 cuthen, kuthen, kithen（意為「熟悉、告知」）的變體，源自中古英語 cuth, couth（意為「熟知、熟悉」），等同於 couth + -le。與中古荷蘭語 kudden（意為「聚集、群聚」）同源。詳見 couth。

etymology.text: Rebracketing of napron (a napron → an apron), from Middle English naperoun, napron, apron, from Old French napperon, diminutive of nappe (“tablecloth”), from Latin mappa (“napkin”). etymology.native: 「napron」的語源來自中古英語 naperoun、napron，意為「圍裙」，源自法語 napperon，是「nappe（桌布）」的縮小形，再源自拉丁語 mappa（餐巾）。其他類似語詞如 adder、daffodil、newt、nickname、orange、trickle、umpire 也有類似語源轉移現象。

etymology.text: From Middle English malencolie, from Old French melancolie, from Ancient Greek μελαγχολία (melankholía, “atrabiliousness”) (from μέλας (mélas), μελαν- (melan-, “black, dark, murky”) + χολή (kholḗ, “bile”)), referring to the humour which ancient Hippocratic and later Galenic medicine associated with sadness and despondency. Compare the Latin ātra bīlis (“black bile”). The adjectival use is a Middle English innovation, perhaps influenced by the suffixes -y, -ly. Doublet of melancholia.
etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 malencolie，來自古法文 melancolie，再來自古希臘文 μελαγχολία（melankholía，意為「憂鬱」），此詞由 μέλας（mélas，意為「黑、暗、混濁」）與 χολή（kholḗ，意為「膽汁」）組成，指古代希波克拉底與蓋倫醫學所稱與悲傷與低落相關的體液。與拉丁文 ātra bīlis（「黑膽汁」）相對。形容詞用法為中世紀英文創新，可能受 -y、-ly 等後綴影響。此詞亦為 melancholia 的同源詞。

senses.definition: An eerie creature or thing.

etymology.native: 「drit」源自中世英文，來自古諾斯語，再溯源自原始日耳曼語，最後源自原始印歐語，意為「排洩物」，與丹麥語、諾爾語、瑞典語、法羅語、冰島語、荷蘭語、低地德語等方言或詞彙同源。

etymology.text: The verb is from Middle English dressen, dresse (“to arrange, put in order”), from Anglo-Norman, Old French dresser, drecier (modern French dresser), from Late Latin *dīrēctiāre (“to guide, direct”), from Classical Latin dīrēctus, whence English direct. Further akin to Latin regō.
etymology.native: 這個動詞來自中古英語 dressen, dresse（意為「整理、排列」），源自盎格魯-諾曼語及古法語 dresser, drecier（現代法語 dresser），來源為拉丁語 *dīrēctiāre（意為「引導、指揮」），再源自古典拉丁語 dīrēctus，與拉丁語 regō 亦有親緣關係。

etymology.native: 「trig」源自古諾斯語 tryggr，意為「忠誠、忠實、真誠」，源自原始日耳曼語 *triwwiz。與古英語 trīewe 同源，意為「忠誠、真誠」。詳見 true。

etymology.native: 源自中世紀英文 closet，來自古法文 closet，由 clos（意為「私密空間」）+ -et（縮小後綴）構成，源自拉丁文 clausum。等同 close + -et，但法文僅用於小型露天圍欄。

etymology.text: From Middle English *hudelen, alteration (due to hudels, hidels (“hiding place”), see hiddle) of *huderen, hoderen (“to cover; press together; huddle”), a frequentative form of Middle English huden, hiden (“to hide”), equivalent to hide + -le and/or hide + -er. Compare Low German huderken (“to brood; coddle; nurse; lull children to sleep”).
etymology.native: 源自中古英語 *hudelen，是 *huderen、hoderen（意為「覆蓋；壓近；聚攏」）的變體，源自中古英語 huden、hiden（意為「隱藏」）的頻繁形式，等同於 hide + -le 和/或 hide + -er。可與低德語 huderken（意為「孵育；撫育；哄睡孩子」）相比。

etymology.text: From Middle French trafique, traffique (“traffic”), from Italian traffico (“traffic”) from trafficare (“to carry on trade”). Potentially from Vulgar Latin *trānsfrīcāre (“to rub across”); Klein instead suggests the Italian has ultimate origin in Arabic تَفْرِيق (tafrīq, “distribution, dispersion”), reshaped to match the native prefix tra- (“trans-”).
etymology.native: 源自中世紀法語 trafique，源自義大利語 traffico，來自拉丁語 trafficare（意為「從事貿易」）。可能來自通俗拉丁語 *trānsfrīcāre（意為「摩擦穿越」）；克萊因則認為義大利語的起源在阿拉伯語 تَفْرِيق（tafrīq，意為「分佈、分散」），並被重新塑造以符合本地前綴 tra-（意為「跨」）

etymology.text: From Middle English wowen, woȝen, from Old English wōgian (“to woo, court, marry”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Scots wow (“to woo”). Perhaps related to Old English wōg, wōh (“bending, crookedness”), in the specific sense of "bend or incline (some)one toward oneself". If so, then derived from Proto-Germanic *wanhō (“a bend, angle”), from Proto-Indo-European *wonk- (“crooked, bent”), from Proto-Indo-European *wā- (“to bend, twist, turn”); related to Old Norse vá (“corner, angle”).
etymology.native: 此詞源自中古英語 wowen, woȝen，來自古英語 wōgian（意為「追求、迎娶」），起源不明。與蘇格蘭語 wow（意為「追求」）同源。可能與古英語 wōg, wōh（意為「彎曲、曲折」）有關，特指「使某人傾向於自己」。若如此，則源自原始日耳曼語 *wanhō（意為「彎曲、角度」），再源自原始印歐語 *wonk-（意為「彎曲、彎折」），而原始印歐語 *wā-（意為「彎曲、扭轉、轉向」）；亦與古諾斯語 vá（意為「角落、角度」）相關。

etymology.text: From Middle English fressh, from Old English fersċ (“fresh, pure, sweet”), from Proto-West Germanic *frisk (“fresh”), from Proto-Germanic *friskaz (“fresh”), from Proto-Indo-European *preysk- (“fresh”). The verb is from Middle English freshen (“to freshen”), from the adjective.
etymology.native: 「fresh」源自中古英語，來源為古英語 fersċ，意為「新鮮、純淨、甜美」，再溯源自西日耳曼語 *frisk，更上溯至古德語 *friskaz，最終源自印歐語系 *preysk-，意為「新鮮」。其動詞則源自中古英語 freshen，即「使新鮮」，來自形容詞。

etymology.native: 這個形容詞來自中古英語 bright，源自古英語 berht、beorht、bryht、byrht，來源於古西日耳曼語 *berht，再溯源自古德語 *berhtaz（意為「明亮」），最終源自印歐語系 *bʰerHǵ-（意為「閃耀、發光、變白」）。

etymology.native: 「man」源自中世紀英文，來自古英文 mann m（意為「人、男子」），再溯源自原始西日耳曼語 *mann，再往上溯源自原始德語 *mann-，最終源自原始印歐語 *mon-（意為「人、男子」）。此詞與 mann 和 Manu 為同源詞。
